purpose: Prepare a peer mesh where Termux agents exchange compact status observations without relaying commands or ADB authority.
authority_boundary: Peer mesh messages are status gossip only.
Peers do not send commands, shell text, ADB pairing material, APK install requests, app launch requests, or cross-headset ADB targets.
The central fleet controller remains the command queue and audit surface.
Central direct ADB remains the recovery and privileged truth-check path.

preflight.label: synthetic-only
preflight.command: Run the peer mesh simulator with synthetic envelopes before adding any network transport.

status.label: summary
status.command: Confirm the summary contains known peers, status, central reachability, and local ADB availability fields only.

status.label: forbidden-message-count
status.command: Confirm forbidden_message_count is zero for public-safe status gossip.

stop.label: no-network
stop.command: No network listener or peer transport is started in this preparation slice.

cleanup.label: public-boundary
cleanup.command: Run python tools/check_public_boundary.py --repo-root . before promoting examples.

evidence: Unit tests for merge, stale, and forbidden-message behavior.

risks.risk: Peer mesh can drift into peer command relay or cross-headset ADB control.
risks.recovery: Reject command-like and shell-like fields in gossip messages and keep command dispatch in the central controller.

risks.risk: Stale peer observations can look like current fleet truth.
risks.recovery: Use per-observation stale_after_seconds and compute alive/stale state in summaries.

risks.risk: Mesh discovery can expose LAN details or real device identities.
risks.recovery: Keep this slice synthetic and promote only redacted or generated agent IDs.

notes: This is preparation for a future mesh. It does not open UDP, mDNS, Bluetooth, MQTT, WebSocket, or HTTP peer listeners.
A later live route should start with gossip-only status over a controlled transport before considering relay behavior.
